newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power moves higher in frigid temps.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power moves higher in frigid temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. moved higher Thursday amid forecasts of continued frigid temperatures Friday and into the weekend, power brokers and marketers said.
Traders reported a wide price disparity through much of the Mid-West, with some desparate utilities paying high prices and others reported to be able to find the odd lower-priced sale.
Forecasts called for temperatures to be 15 to 25 degrees Fahrenheit below normal in much of the region throuugh the weekend with expectations of a return to more normal temperatures early next week.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday moved higher to $40-46.00 from $27.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $15.00-18.00 per MWh, with very little off-peak power said to be traded.
February ECAR was said to have held steady at $23.50-24.00.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), where temperatures were reaching highs under the zero degrees Fahrenheit mark, peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery were discussed at $32.00-43.00 from $38.00-39.50 on Wednesday for Thursday delivery, the sources said.
Off-peak next day non-firm MAPP power was steady to higher at $16.00-19.00 from $15.00-19.00 on Wednesday.

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Friday were talked in a very large range from $35.00-50.00, with unconfirmed trades reported at both sides of the spectrum.
MAIN peak next day power had been talked at $27.00-29.00 on Wednesday.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to be steady at $17.00-19.00 per MWh.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Friday delivery was talked at $44.00-50.00 in the south of the region, while prices were pegged at $36.00-40.00 in the north of SPP.
SPP peak next-day power had been trading at $27.00-31.00 through the region on Wednesday.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady to higher at $17.00-20.00 from $17.00-19.00 per MWh on Wednesday.
February SPP was said to have eased to the $23.00-24.00 range from $24.00-24.25 on Wednesday, the sources said.
